title: Twelve DCU tasks report the identical 0.005439 ms for both arms while moving 1.0 to 1.5 MiB, so at the default shape the paired assay cannot discriminate

observation:
Twelve operators of different arithmetic report the identical pooled median, to six decimal places, for both arms. The byte counts settle what kind of floor it is: silu moves 1.000 MiB and softmax_backward 1.500, half again as much, and both take 0.005439 ms. Bandwidth-bound work does not do that.

A footprint sweep on the same device says where the floor ends: duration is flat at about 2.4 us below 1 MiB and tracks bytes from about 8 MiB. The task shapes sit in the flat region. So for those twelve the comparison cannot work -- a candidate that halved the arithmetic and one that doubled it would both report 0.005439, and the paired assay would call both close_null.

This record's counts have been wrong twice and the corrections belong in it. It first said seven, then eleven; the enumeration behind the eleven listed seven tasks and then four more with selu named in both, a union of ten. Recounting from the collected medians rather than from the previous sentence gives twelve. It also said that only three runs rose above the floor and that all three showed the candidate losing: fourteen separated, and among them three candidates beat their baseline by more than the declared 1.05 materiality (F-2026-09-18-005). Both claims were arithmetic about a table, made without redoing the arithmetic.

What the separated runs establish is the useful half: the assay resolves this hardware when the kernels cost enough to be resolved. The floor is what these particular kernels cost at this footprint, not the assay declining to resolve anything.
proposed_change:
Run one task at several shapes on this target and read where the reported time starts tracking the bytes -- that is the smallest experiment that distinguishes a dispatch floor from a small kernel, and it needs no Compiler or Lab change. If the times separate at a larger shape, the DCU task shapes should be chosen above that point, and the choice recorded with the measurement that justified it rather than inherited from the CUDA defaults.

Do not read the twelve close_null results as evidence that the authored candidates matched their baselines. They are evidence that the assay could not tell, which is a different statement and the one the receipts support. A campaign at a shape below the discriminating range spends provider budget to learn nothing about latency, and that is worth knowing before a sweep rather than after.

This says nothing about correctness: all seven passed their five validation cases against the external oracle, and that half of the evaluation is unaffected by the floor.
